reasoning: Base n=1 gives determinant 1 and empty product 1. For n>=2 subtract row 1 from rows 2..n and expand in the first column. Factor (x_i-x_1) from each remaining row. The residual k-th column evaluates p_{k-1}(t)=t^{k-1}+x_1t^{k-2}+...+x_1^{k-1} at t=x_i. For k descending, replace column k by column k-x_1 times column k-1; this yields the ordinary Vandermonde matrix on x_2,...,x_n. Apply induction and combine factors. This proof never divides, so repeated x_i cause no exceptional case.
